title.zh: 公元313年 · 米兰的宗教宽容措施

location.label: Milan; representative setting named Mediolanum in the translated account

labelI18n.en: Milan; representative setting named Mediolanum in the translated account
labelI18n.zh: 米兰；翻译文献中称作梅迪奥拉努姆的代表地点

summary.en:
A translated account of the 313 arrangements associated with Milan names Constantine and Licinius and sets out freedom of worship for Christians and people of other religions. It also directs the return of property belonging to Christian communities. These measures followed an earlier toleration edict issued under Galerius in 311.

A statement of imperial policy does not prove that every official implemented it immediately or that all religious persecution ended everywhere. Nor did the 313 arrangements make Christianity the official religion of the Roman Empire. The 325 Council of Nicaea was a later and different event. Milan identifies the setting in the translated account, not the boundaries of a religious community.
summary.zh:
一份关于313年米兰相关措施的翻译文献提到君士坦丁与李锡尼，提出给予基督徒及其他宗教信众礼拜自由，并要求归还基督徒社群的财产。这些措施发生在伽列里乌于311年颁布较早的宽容敕令之后。

帝国政策的声明不能证明所有官员立即执行，也不能证明各地宗教迫害全部结束。313年的措施也没有使基督教成为罗马帝国的官方宗教。325年尼西亚会议是后来的另一事件。米兰是翻译文献所述的背景地点，并非宗教社群的边界。

dateNote.en: 313 CE is the focus of the translated toleration account; it differs from the 311 edict, the 325 council and later policies.
dateNote.zh: 公元313年是所引宽容措施译文的关注节点，有别于311年敕令、325年会议及后来的政策。

sources.title: Galerius and Constantine: Edicts of Toleration 311/313 AD
sources.publisher: Internet History Sourcebooks Project, hosted by Fordham University
sources.evidenceNote: Directly inspected the 313 section translating Lactantius, chapter 48: Constantine and Licinius meet near Mediolanum, allow Christians and others freedom of worship, and direct restoration of Christian communal property. This is a later translated literary transmission; declared policy does not prove consistent implementation or that all persecution stopped.

sources.title: Politics and the world of faith in late antiquity – 1700 years of the Council of Nicaea
sources.publisher: Nisa Iduna Kirchengast / Roman City of Carnuntum
sources.evidenceNote: Directly inspected the museum’s 2025 exhibition explainer: it dates the 313 Milan toleration policy and Constantine’s council at Nicaea to 325, and describes bishops’ debate over Arius and a creed. Its broad statement that persecution ended is not treated as proof that all persecution stopped everywhere.

reviewLimit.en: The online edition reproduces a translation of Lactantius rather than a separately inspected original inscription; its declaration must not be equated with uniform local enforcement.
reviewLimit.zh: 网络版本转载拉克坦提乌斯文本的译文，并非另行查阅的原始铭刻；其中声明不能等同于各地一致执行。

title.zh: 公元325年 · 尼西亚会议

location.label: Nicaea, present-day İznik; representative location of the council

labelI18n.en: Nicaea, present-day İznik; representative location of the council
labelI18n.zh: 尼西亚，即今伊兹尼克；会议的代表地点

summary.en:
In 325 CE, Constantine convened a council of bishops at Nicaea. The Carnuntum museum account describes debates associated with Arius and the adoption of a creed. This meeting brought imperial power and Christian theological argument together, but did not mark the beginning of Christianity or make all Christian communities immediately agree.

The council followed changes in Roman policy toward Christians, including toleration measures associated with Milan in 313. A council’s decisions and later responses belong to a longer history of debate, institutions and political power. Nicaea is the location of the meeting, not a map of a uniform Christian population or religious boundary.
summary.zh:
公元325年，君士坦丁在尼西亚召集主教会议。卡农图姆博物馆的叙述介绍了与阿里乌有关的争论及信经的制定。这次会议将帝国权力与基督教神学论辩联系起来，但它不是基督教的起点，也没有使所有基督徒社群立即达成一致。

会议发生在罗马对基督徒政策变化之后，其中包括与313年米兰相关的宽容措施。会议决定及后续反应属于有关争论、制度与政治权力的更长历史。尼西亚是会议地点，并非整齐划一的基督徒人口分布图或宗教疆界。

dateNote.en: 325 CE marks the council, not Christianity’s founding or the endpoint of Christian theological disagreement.
dateNote.zh: 公元325年标记这次会议，不是基督教的创立或神学争论的终点。

sources.title: Politics and the world of faith in late antiquity – 1700 years of the Council of Nicaea
sources.publisher: Nisa Iduna Kirchengast / Roman City of Carnuntum
sources.evidenceNote: Directly inspected the museum’s 2025 exhibition explainer: it dates the 313 Milan toleration policy and Constantine’s council at Nicaea to 325, and describes bishops’ debate over Arius and a creed. Its broad statement that persecution ended is not treated as proof that all persecution stopped everywhere.

sources.title: The Beginnings of Christianity as an Integral Part of Early Judaism
sources.publisher: Markus Tiwald / The Bible and Interpretation, University of Arizona
sources.evidenceNote: Directly inspected the scholarly essay on Jesus and his first followers within diverse first-century Judaism and on long, regionally uneven Christian–Jewish differentiation. The author’s extended chronology and interpretations are a scholarly argument, not a universally agreed separation date.

reviewLimit.en: The museum provides an introductory account of the meeting; the creed’s reception and theological interpretations varied and require specialist historical and community perspectives.
reviewLimit.zh: 博物馆提供会议的入门叙述；信经接受情况和神学解释各不相同，需要专业史学与社群视角。

title.en: Late Roman government and the western imperial endpoint
title.zh: 晚期罗马政府与西部帝位的终结

summary.en:
Diocletian’s reforms and the experiment of rule by several emperors addressed the problems of governing and defending a large empire. Constantine later reunited imperial power and established Constantinople as a new capital. These changes shifted the distribution of courts, military resources and religious patronage; they were not a simple movement of an unchanged capital from one city to another.

The western empire’s fifth-century troubles involved armies, rival courts, migration, warfare and the creation of new kingdoms. In 476 Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus, a conventional endpoint for the western imperial office. Roman law, Christianity, urban communities and administrative practices continued in different settings, while the eastern Roman government survived. Reading this political phase alongside provincial evidence helps distinguish an imperial deposition from the end of all Roman social life.
summary.zh:
戴克里先的改革与多皇帝共治实验，回应了治理和保卫大帝国的困难。君士坦丁后来重新集中帝权，并建立新都君士坦丁堡。这些变化重新配置宫廷、军力和宗教资助，并不是一个始终不变的首都从一城搬到另一城。

西部帝国在五世纪的困境涉及军队、竞争的宫廷、迁徙、战争与新王国的形成。476年，奥多亚塞废黜罗慕路斯·奥古斯都鲁斯，通常被用作西部帝位的终点。罗马法律、基督教、城市群体和行政做法仍在不同环境下延续，东部罗马政府也继续存在。把这一政治阶段与行省证据并读，有助于区分皇帝被废与整个罗马社会生活的终结。

dateNote.en: Focus: 284–476, with western government as the terminal reference; eastern continuity is shown separately. Ravenna is a representative later court.
dateNote.zh: 关注284—476年，终点指西部政府；东部延续另列。拉文纳是后期宫廷的代表点。

sources.evidenceNote: Imperial institutions, Diocletian and Constantine, western deposition in 476 and eastern continuity. Retrieval: full-page text inspected.

sources.evidenceNote: Provincial military and civilian setting; broad imperial context. Retrieval: indexed institutional text inspected; full-page not retrieved in this batch.

title.en: Abu Simbel: rebuilding monuments above the reservoir
title.zh: 阿布辛贝：在水库上方重建古迹

location.label: Relocated Abu Simbel temples, Egypt; representative modern site point

summary.en: The temples of Abu Simbel reopened in September 1968 after an international project cut them into numbered blocks and reassembled them above the rising waters associated with the Aswan High Dam. Engineers recreated the cliff setting while moving the monuments uphill and inland. The operation followed appeals by Egypt and Sudan and formed one part of a much wider campaign to safeguard Nubian monuments. It is a useful example of how twentieth-century infrastructure altered an ancient landscape and prompted new forms of international heritage cooperation. The date marks the relocated temples’ reopening, not their ancient construction or the completion of every Nubian rescue project.
summary.zh: 阿布辛贝神庙于1968年9月重新开放。此前的国际工程把神庙切割成编号石块，在高于阿斯旺高坝蓄水水位的地方重新组装，并重建崖壁环境，将古迹向高处和内陆迁移。这项行动响应埃及与苏丹的请求，是抢救努比亚古迹的大规模计划的一部分。它说明二十世纪基础设施如何改变古老景观，并推动新的国际遗产合作。这里的日期指搬迁后神庙重新开放，不是神庙在古代的建造时间，也不表示全部努比亚抢救工程已经完成。

dateNote.en: The relocated temples reopened on 22 September 1968. The broader Nubian campaign ran from 1960 to 1980, with other monuments moved on different schedules. The point marks the relocated site.
dateNote.zh: 搬迁后的神庙于1968年9月22日重新开放。更广泛的努比亚抢救行动持续于1960—1980年，其他古迹有各自的搬迁时间。点位标示重建后的地点。

sources.title: The story of Abu Simbel
sources.evidenceNote: Institutional project history documents the international appeal, engineering method, new site and reopening on 22 September 1968; distinguishes later Philae work.

sources.title: Nubian Monuments from Abu Simbel to Philae
sources.evidenceNote: Heritage synthesis relates the ancient monuments to the international safeguarding campaign of 1960–1980.

en: Numbered stone blocks allowed the temples to be dismantled and reassembled.
Abu Simbel was one project within a wider Nubian heritage campaign.
zh: 编号石块使拆解和重新组装神庙成为可能。
阿布辛贝只是更广泛的努比亚遗产抢救行动之一。

title.en: Capetians: assembling royal power in France
title.zh: 卡佩王朝：法国王权的逐步整合

summary.en:
Capetian kings began with authority contested by powerful regional lords. Across the following centuries, royal government expanded its reach within the kingdom of France. The history involves negotiation, warfare and institutions rather than the sudden appearance of a fully formed modern nation.

Royal religious patronage and the rebuilding of churches helped express authority. The Met’s chronology highlights Philip II, Louis IX and Philip IV as rulers associated with this expansion. The direct Capetian line ended in 1328, while the Valois branch continued a related royal lineage. A dynastic change therefore need not mark the end of the kingdom.
summary.zh:
卡佩诸王起初的权威受到强大地方领主限制。随后数百年，王室政府逐渐扩大在法兰西王国内的影响。这段历史涉及协商、战争和制度建设，而不是一个完整现代民族国家突然出现。

王室宗教资助与教堂重建帮助表达权威。大都会年表特别强调腓力二世、路易九世和腓力四世与王权扩展的关系。卡佩直系于1328年终结，瓦卢瓦支系继续同一家族谱系。因此王朝支系更替并不一定意味着王国灭亡。

dateNote.en: 987–1328 represents the direct Capetian royal line; cadet branches ruled later. Paris is a representative center, not the extent of royal control in every year.
dateNote.zh: 987—1328年指卡佩直系王朝，其旁支此后继续统治。巴黎为代表性中心，不表示王室在每一年控制的全部范围。

sources.title: France, 1000–1400 A.D.
sources.evidenceNote: Provides direct dynastic dates, regional lords and growth of royal authority.

en: The kingdom and the direct royal line have different endpoints.
Royal authority grew within a landscape of powerful regional lords.
zh: 王国与王室直系具有不同终点。
王权在强大地方领主并存的环境中成长。

title.en: Habsburg monarchy: a collection of crowns and laws
title.zh: 哈布斯堡君主国：多顶王冠与多种法律

summary.en:
Habsburg authority in central Europe grew through inheritance, marriage, election and war. Ferdinand’s acquisition of the Bohemian and Hungarian crowns in 1526 helped form a composite monarchy anchored in the Austrian hereditary lands. Possessing a crown did not ensure uncontested rule over every part of its claimed kingdom, particularly in lands contested with the Ottomans.

Different estates, languages and legal traditions persisted within the ruler’s domains. The dynasty’s imperial role in the Holy Roman Empire overlapped with, but was distinct from, these hereditary possessions. Political integration was a process of bargaining and administrative change rather than the instant creation of one uniform country. The Austrian imperial title adopted in 1804 provides this entry’s terminal transition. Reading the monarchy alongside Ottoman and regional histories clarifies how central Europe’s borders and institutions changed without reducing those histories to one dynasty’s family tree.
summary.zh:
哈布斯堡在中欧的权力通过继承、婚姻、选举和战争发展。1526年斐迪南取得波希米亚及匈牙利王冠，推动形成以奥地利世袭领地为基础的复合君主国。拥有王冠，并不表示对所声称王国的全部地区都能实施无争议统治，在与奥斯曼竞争的地区尤其如此。

统治者领地内仍保留不同的等级会议、语言和法律传统。王朝在神圣罗马帝国中的帝位，与这些世袭领地重叠，却并不相同。政治整合是一系列协商和行政变革，并非瞬间建立一个均质国家。1804年采用奥地利帝号，构成本条的阶段转折。把君主国与奥斯曼及各地区历史并读，有助于解释中欧边界和制度如何变化，而不把这些历史缩成一个家族的谱系。

dateNote.en: Focus: 1526 dynastic acquisitions to the Austrian imperial title in 1804; this is not the start of the Habsburg family or an unchanged territory.
dateNote.zh: 关注1526年王朝取得王冠至1804年采用奥地利帝号；并非哈布斯堡家族的起点，也不表示疆域不变。

title.en: Holy Roman Empire: institutions across many territories
title.zh: 神圣罗马帝国：诸领地之间的制度

summary.en:
The Holy Roman Empire linked rulers, bishoprics, cities and other territories through an imperial office and a changing body of law. It was multilingual and decentralized; an elected emperor did not govern every territory as a provincial administrator. Imperial assemblies, courts and negotiated privileges gave this political order practical forms beyond coronations and dynastic portraits.

Religious division, territorial ambitions and the strength of princes reshaped the empire without immediately dissolving it. Habsburg hereditary lands overlapped with imperial politics but were not identical to the empire. The structure ended when Francis II relinquished the imperial crown in 1806. Using a single overview makes these institutional continuities legible while regional histories explain differences within them. Neither a modern German outline nor the ruler’s family possessions can substitute for the empire’s changing membership.
summary.zh:
神圣罗马帝国通过帝位和不断变化的法律，把诸侯、主教领、城市及其他领地联系起来。它具有多语言和分权特征；经选举产生的皇帝并不把所有领地都当作行省直接管理。帝国会议、法院及协商形成的特权，使这一政治秩序拥有加冕礼与王朝肖像之外的实际制度。

宗教分裂、领土诉求和诸侯力量不断改变帝国，却没有使它立即解体。哈布斯堡世袭领地与帝国政治重叠，但两者并不相同。1806年，弗朗茨二世放弃帝冠，这一结构走向终结。总览条目呈现制度延续，区域历史则解释内部差异。现代德国轮廓或统治者家族的全部领地，都不能替代不断变化的帝国成员范围。

dateNote.en: 962–1806 follows the German Historical Museum convention; Charlemagne’s 800 coronation is an earlier antecedent, not denied by this focus.
dateNote.zh: 962—1806年采用德国历史博物馆的分期；800年查理曼加冕是更早的前史，并未因此被排除。

It was multilingual and decentralized; an elected emperor did not govern every territory as a provincial administrator.

它具有多语言和分权特征；经选举产生的皇帝并不把所有领地都当作行省直接管理。

title.en: 70 CE · Jerusalem’s Second Temple is destroyed
title.zh: 公元70年 · 耶路撒冷第二圣殿被毁

location.label: Jerusalem; representative setting of the Temple destruction

labelI18n.en: Jerusalem; representative setting of the Temple destruction
labelI18n.zh: 耶路撒冷；圣殿被毁的代表地点

summary.en:
During the Roman siege of Jerusalem in 70 CE, the Second Temple was destroyed. The event profoundly affected Jewish religious institutions and communities, but the city’s destruction does not mark a single beginning of the Jewish diaspora: Jewish communities had already lived outside the land for centuries. Jewish life also continued within the land.

Later rabbinic texts preserve accounts of people and decisions associated with the aftermath. Rabba Alieza Salzberg Yizhar cautions that the familiar story of Yohanan ben Zakkai escaping in a coffin should not be accepted uncritically as a contemporaneous report. The historical event and later literary tradition provide different kinds of evidence.
summary.zh:
公元70年罗马围攻耶路撒冷期间，第二圣殿被毁。此事深刻影响犹太宗教制度与社群，但不能将城市遭毁视为犹太离散唯一的开始：此前数百年，已有犹太社群生活在故土之外，故土内的犹太生活也继续。

后世拉比文献保存了与其后局势相关的人物和决定的叙述。拉比阿莉扎·萨尔茨贝格·伊兹哈尔提醒，关于约哈南·本·扎凯藏身棺材逃出的熟悉故事，不应未经审视就当作同时代报道。历史事件与后来的文学传统提供不同类型的证据。

dateNote.en: 70 CE marks the siege and destruction of the Temple. It is neither the beginning of all diaspora nor the end of Judaism.
dateNote.zh: 公元70年标记围城与圣殿被毁，既不是所有离散的开始，也不是犹太教的终结。

sources.title: Judaism after the Temple
sources.publisher: Rabba Alieza Salzberg Yizhar / My Jewish Learning
sources.evidenceNote: Directly inspected the account of the Roman siege and destruction of the Second Temple in 70 CE, later Torah study and Jewish law in different places, and the rabbinic story of Yohanan ben Zakkai’s escape and Yavneh. The author explicitly questions whether that story can be treated as straightforward history.

sources.title: Jewish Art in Late Antiquity and Early Byzantium
sources.publisher: Barbara Drake Boehm and Melanie Holcomb / The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.evidenceNote: Directly inspected the art-historical essay’s discussion of Jewish communities in Roman regions, the destruction of the Jerusalem Temple in 70 CE and the third-century synagogue at Dura-Europos beside a Christian meeting house. Material remains are selective evidence, not a single starting date for diaspora.

sources.title: 539 BCE to 632 CE: The Story
sources.evidenceNote: Directly inspected the educational overview on Jewish exile before Cyrus’s 539 BCE conquest, different returns, people who had not been exiled and communities in Egypt and Asia Minor. Its broad political chronology is simplified; a claim about Christian imperialization was not adopted.

reviewLimit.en: The inspected Jewish educational and museum accounts cover the destruction and selected later interpretations; they do not resolve every detail of the siege or reconstruct a border.
reviewLimit.zh: 已查阅的犹太教育与博物馆资料涵盖圣殿被毁和部分后世解释；不能解决围城的每个细节，也不复原疆界。

title.en: Konbaung: royal expansion and colonial conquest
title.zh: 贡榜王朝：王室扩张与殖民征服

summary.en:
The Konbaung dynasty emerged in central Myanmar in 1752 and expanded across much of the region. Its rulers moved their capitals over time; Mandalay became the final royal center. Royal diplomacy, Buddhist patronage and warfare linked the court to neighbors and distant powers.

Expansion brought the kingdom into conflict with British-ruled India. Three Anglo-Burmese wars progressively removed territory and ended the monarchy in 1885. Royal chronicles and administrative orders provide evidence for this period, but each was produced for particular purposes. The end of the dynasty must be separated from the much longer histories of Myanmar’s diverse communities.
summary.zh:
贡榜王朝于1752年兴起于今缅甸中部，并向区域多处扩张。统治者曾多次迁都，曼德勒成为最后的王室中心。外交、佛教资助与战争，把宫廷连接到邻国和远方势力。

扩张使王国与英国统治的印度发生冲突。三次英缅战争逐步夺去领土，并于1885年终结君主制。王室编年史和行政命令为该时期提供证据，但各类文书都有特定制作目的。王朝终点需要与缅甸多元社区更长久的历史区分。

dateNote.en: 1752–1885 is the conventional dynastic interval. Mandalay was only the final capital, not the dynasty’s capital from its beginning. The endpoint marks overthrow of the monarchy, not an end to resistance or community histories.
dateNote.zh: 1752—1885年为通行王朝时段。曼德勒只是末期首都，并非从创立之初即为都。终点标记君主制被推翻，不表示抵抗或社区历史结束。

catalogueMetadata.name: Medal of Emperor Rudolf II (1552-1612)
catalogueMetadata.description:
Since antiquity, rulers have minted coins and medals to celebrate their power and dominion. On this gold medal from about 1600, the Habsburg Emperor Rudolf II wears a laurel wreath, a sign of victory and peace, and the chain and pendant of the Order of the Golden Fleece. The Latin inscription on the front,  RUDOLPHUS II ROM IMP AUG REX HUNG BOE , declares Rudolf the Supreme Emperor of the Romans, King of Hungary and Bohemia. On the reverse, a ram, zodiac sign of the constellation Capricorn, refers to Augustus Caesar, who was conceived under this sign, suggesting an analogy between Rudolf and Caesar. The Latin inscription,  ASTRUM FULGET CAES  (The Emperor's Star Shines Brightly), along with the symbols of the twinkling star, the earth, and the Habsburg eagle, suggest Rudolf's supremacy and the prosperous future of the Habsburg dynasty.   
 The emperor's elegant three-quarter pose and the subtle differentiation of textures on the medal demonstrate the high quality of the casting. The hair is suggested by blunt troughs and lines, the emperor's ruffle has the illusion of depth, and the skin is polished smooth, while the drapery's thick folds effectively suggest heavy fabric.

catalogueMetadata.name: The Destruction of Jerusalem
catalogueMetadata.description: In the miniature depicting the Siege of Jerusalem in 70 A.D., the Roman Emperor Titus, who directed the battle, sits enthroned in a tent while his soldiers storm the city. As is typical for the art of this period, the scene is anachronistic: the figures wear armor of the 1400s, and the city of Jerusalem is a medieval walled city with battlements, wood-and-plaster houses, and even a Gothic church. To give the illusion of recessed space, the artist used an intuitive rather than a mathematical perspective, stacking the farther buildings on top of those in the front. Despite this innovative method for representing space, he also used an un-naturalistic background of checkered squares for the sky, instead of blue paint. This miniature complements the only other full-page miniature in the manuscript, "Adam and Eve," implying a parallel between The Fall and the eventual destruction of Jerusalem. Just as Adam and Eve were punished for disobeying God, medieval Christians believed that the destruction of Jerusalem resulted from the Jews' failure to accept Jesus as the Messiah.

ownerReview: All six full images individually viewed. Coin and medal inscriptions and catalogue descriptions match their subjects. Jerusalem is a medieval Christian depiction of 70 CE; its anti-Jewish theological framing is attributed to the later manuscript, not asserted as history. Abu Simbel is a pre-relocation nineteenth-century photograph, Sainte-Chapelle a later view of royal patronage, and Mandalay a documented post-annexation monastery reuse. The two representation enums were corrected to object-photograph and manuscript-detail without changing date or interpretation. Redundant source links removed. No UNESCO retry or new retrieval claim.
